audit.whatIsWrong: Level 3 and Levels 4-5 are assigned to Gnar in both layers while their own whys say the lane flips to Dr. Mundo at 3; First item and 2+ items sit on 'Skill' while their whys and spikes say Dr. Mundo out-sustains Mini Gnar outright. whys[4] and whys[5] are also shifted one row out of phase with their labels.
audit.why: Dr. Mundo wins 53.91% over 1293 games and the packet chart reads Gnar, Gnar, Dr. Mundo, Dr. Mundo, Skill, Dr. Mundo, Dr. Mundo — which is exactly what the prose on this page already argues.
audit.corrected: Levels 1-2 Gnar, Level 3 and Levels 4-5 Dr. Mundo, Level 6 Skill (Rage-dependent), First item and 2+ items Dr. Mundo, with ratings and whys realigned.

audit.whatIsWrong: The matchup-defining cooldown is printed as '(—)' in breakdown.cooldowns and report[5].t — no number at all. Boomerang Throw (16/14.5/13/11.5/10), Hop (22/19.5/17/14.5/12), Wallop (7s) and GNAR! (90/60/30) are all absent.
audit.why: Every 'commit on its cooldown' line on the page is unusable without the number, and GNAR! going from 90s at rank 1 to 30s at rank 3 completely changes how often you can be caught.
audit.corrected: R written as 90s at rank 1 / 30s at rank 3, Wallop as 7s, Q as 16s at rank 1 with the catch refund noted, Hop as 22s at rank 1.
sources: champ-data/_kits gnar Q/W/E/R cd fields and Q text (catching reduces cooldown)

audit.whatIsWrong: Nothing states the condition on GNAR!: enemies are only stunned if they hit a wall. The page treats it as a flat stun. Nothing notes that Dr. Mundo has no dash, so terrain decides whether that ult is a slow or a full lockdown, and the passive resisting the first immobilizing effect is never tied to Wallop or the wall-slam. 'Q sustain' is again credited to Infected Bonesaw, which heals nothing.
audit.why: Riot's text: 'Any enemy that hits a wall is stunned and takes bonus damage.' Standing in open ground downgrades his ult to a knock-back and slow, which is the single biggest lever a Mundo has in this lane; the same text is why Flash should be saved for the wall, not the damage.
audit.corrected: GNAR! stuns only on a wall hit — fight in open ground; Mega Wallop is the reliable stun on 7s; the passive absorbs one of them; healing re-attributed to Heart Zapper's end-of-duration burst.

edits.before: At 3 your Q sustain and E punish flip the lane to you.
edits.after: At 3 Heart Zapper's burst heal flips the lane to you.

edits.before: At 5 it's even — his Mega Rage burst window balances your sustain.
edits.after: At 6 his Rage bar, not the level, sets the burst window — Skill.

edits.before: Level 6 leans to you; he can't reliably access Mega in lane.
edits.after: First item's HP stack out-lasts Mini poke — Dr. Mundo.

edits.before: Mini Gnar kites you early with Q Boomerang Throw and W Hyper on-hit, but by level 3 your Q Infected Bonesaw sustains the poke and E Blunt Force Trauma punishes any auto-attack step-in. Close the gap when his Q is on cooldown and his E Hop isn't up to escape.
edits.after: Mini Gnar kites you early with Boomerang Throw (Q) and Hyper (W) on-hit, but by level 3 Heart Zapper's burst heals the poke back and Blunt Force punishes any auto step-in. His Q is 16s at rank 1 and refunds if he catches it — close when he misses and his 22s Hop is spent.

edits.before: Level 6 stays even because it's really about his Rage bar, not levels — Mega Gnar's GNAR! (R) plus W stun can chunk you, but he has no reliable ult in lane at will. Watch his Rage; when he's Mini and low on Rage, all-in freely.
edits.after: Level 6 is about his Rage bar, not his level. GNAR! (R) is 90s at rank 1 and only stuns enemies it slams into a wall, while Mega Wallop stuns every 7s — your passive absorbs the first of those. Fight in open ground, and all-in while he is Mini.

edits.before: Mini Gnar kites you at levels 1-2 with Q Boomerang Throw and W Hyper on-hit poke, so eat some chip and farm. From level 3 you stabilize — Q Infected Bonesaw sustains the harass and E Blunt Force Trauma punishes every auto step-in. Close when his Q is down and his E Hop can't reset the spacing.
edits.after: Mini Gnar kites you at levels 1-2 with Boomerang Throw (Q) and Hyper (W) on-hit poke, so eat some chip and farm. From level 3 you stabilize — Heart Zapper's end burst heals the harass back and Blunt Force punishes every auto step-in. Close when his Q misses, as catching it refunds its 16s cooldown, and his 22s Hop is spent.

edits.before: Late you out-sustain Mini Gnar's kiting completely and just manage the Mega burst. Fight him while he's Mini, bait the E Hop before you commit your Q slow, and if he transforms mid-skirmish, peel out with R Maximum Dosage move speed and re-engage once it's spent.
edits.after: Late you out-sustain Mini Gnar's kiting completely and just manage the Mega burst. Fight him in open ground — you have no dash, and a wall behind you is what turns GNAR! from a knock-back into a stun. Bait the Hop, and if he transforms mid-skirmish peel out on Maximum Dosage's move speed.

edits.before: - Gnar GNAR! (Mega Stun) (—): matchup-defining — His Mega all-in. Don’t fight transform. Track it before every commit. - Your ultimate: spend it on kill windows, never on waves. - Summoners: track his Flash after any close call — it changes every dive call.
edits.after: - Gnar GNAR! (90s at rank 1, 30s at rank 3): matchup-defining — it only stuns if it slams you into a wall, so fight in open ground. - Mega Wallop (W, 7s) is his other stun, and your passive absorbs one of them. - Your ultimate (120s): spend it on kill windows, never on waves.

edits.before: Track Gnar’s GNAR! (Mega Stun) (—): His Mega all-in. Don’t fight transform. It’s down or you don’t go.
edits.after: Track Gnar’s GNAR! (90s at rank 1, 30s at rank 3): it stuns only if a wall is behind you — fight in the open.

edits.before: Transform to Mega Gnar for GNAR! stun burst
edits.after: Slam you into a wall with GNAR! for the stun
